Coating Challenges in Manufacturing & Automation

Manufacturing powder coating must survive daily abuse, repeated cleaning and long production runs without flaking or fading. The main challenges are corrosion from coolant and washdown, abrasion from moving product, inconsistent colour between batches, and tight delivery windows that leave little room for rework.

Powder coating for automation equipment is demanding because frames, conveyor structures and enclosures combine thick welded joints with thin sheet sections, and those areas heat at different rates in the oven. Oils, mill scale and weld spatter block adhesion unless they are removed first. Hollow tubing can trap moisture, while threaded holes and bearing surfaces need precise masking. Powder coating for manufacturers solves these problems when preparation, powder choice and oven loading are planned together instead of treated as separate steps.

Schedule is the other pressure. A line waiting on guards or bases cannot ship, so a finisher has to hold a dependable lead time and speak up early when a part needs extra work. Powder coating for manufacturing succeeds or fails on consistency. Repeat orders depend on batch consistency: the same powder, the same preparation and the same cure every time, so a replacement panel ordered next year still matches the original.
Parts and Metals We Coat for Production Equipment

We coat welded steel, aluminum and fabricated assemblies used in production equipment, including conveyor frames, automation line frames, robotic bases, machine guards, chutes, brackets and enclosures. Parts range from small production batches up to large structures within our 6,000 lb capacity.

Mild steel is the most common metal in manufacturing powder coating, and it responds well to blasting and phosphate pre-treatment before coating. Aluminum covers, plates and guards are cleaned and prepared differently so the powder bonds without trapping gases. Galvanized and stainless parts can also be finished, but they need a conversation about surface condition first. Our powder coating for manufacturers program covers the following parts:

items: Conveyor frames and support structures for plant lines
Automation line frames, cell guarding and safety fencing
Robotic bases, mounting plates and machine pedestals
Machine guards, covers, hoppers and chutes
Brackets, weldments and enclosures made in repeat batches

blocks.text: Weight and geometry matter as much as the metal. Long frames, wide enclosures and heavy bases are racked so powder reaches every weld and corner, and parts are supported during curing to prevent distortion. Machine guard powder coating on thin sheet gets extra care to avoid warping.

Large fabrications go into our oversized oven, and our [capabilities page](/capabilities) lists current size and weight limits so engineers can check a part before sending it. We can also coat small components together with larger frames in one order, which keeps an assembly's colour consistent across every piece.
Finishes and Specifications for Production Equipment

Most production equipment powder coating uses a thermoset polyester, epoxy or hybrid powder, applied by electrostatic spray and cured in the oven at roughly 180–200 °C. We match RAL colour codes and customer samples, and offer textured finishes alongside matte, gloss and metallic.

Choosing the right finish is part of powder coating for manufacturers done well. Texture is a practical choice for machine guard powder coating because it hides weld marks and minor handling scratches, while gloss wipes clean more easily. Corporate colours, safety yellow for guards and neutral greys for frames can all be matched and recorded, so a later order uses the same code. If equipment will be installed outdoors or exposed to chemicals, tell us early, because that changes which powder we recommend.

Polyester powders are a common choice for general equipment, epoxy suits indoor parts that need hardness and chemical resistance, and hybrids balance the two. We recommend a powder after reviewing the working environment, not before, so manufacturing powder coating decisions rest on how the part will actually be used.

Quality is checked, not assumed. Coating thickness is measured with a calibrated gauge following ASTM D7091, adhesion can be tested to ASTM D3359, and corrosion performance can be rated with ASTM B117 salt spray testing when a project calls for it. Test reports are available on request, and our quality steps are documented with the Absolute Bureau of Certification.

Tight tolerances get special attention. Threaded holes, bearing seats and ground surfaces are masked with plugs and tape so the finish never interferes with assembly. Tell us which surfaces must stay bare, and we will mark them on the work order before coating starts.
How We Work With Manufacturing Teams

Our manufacturer powder coating process runs from quote to delivery in a fixed sequence: inspection, preparation, masking, coating, curing, quality check and packaging. Standard orders leave in 48 hours, and our shop is open Monday to Friday, 7 AM to 5 PM.

items: Send drawings, photos or a sample part with the quantity, metal and colour code.
We inspect the parts and confirm the prep method, powder and delivery timing in writing.
Parts are cleaned, blasted if needed, pre-treated and masked.
Powder is applied by electrostatic spray and cured in the oven.
Each batch is inspected, then packed to prevent scratches in transit.
You pick up at our Milton shop, or we arrange delivery.

Services Manufacturers Combine

Manufacturing customers usually pair coating with preparation and, for large orders, with scheduled production runs. The services below are the ones most often combined on a single work order, so each job stays simple.

Our [industrial powder coating](/services/industrial-powder-coating) service covers heavy structures and machine components. [Surface preparation and pretreatment](/services/surface-preparation) handles degreasing, phosphate treatment and masking, which determines how well the powder bonds. [Sandblasting](/services/sandblasting) removes rust, mill scale and old coatings from fabricated parts, and mobile blasting is available for equipment that cannot be moved easily. For recurring programs, our [bulk and commercial orders](/services/bulk-commercial-orders) service sets up repeat batches with consistent preparation and colour. Together these services make powder coating for manufacturing a one-supplier job, from raw fabrications to assembly-ready parts. Teams that finish frames in volume often start with preparation and blasting, then move to a repeating schedule once the first batch is approved, which makes production equipment powder coating predictable from one order to the next.

Manufacturing & Automation FAQs

Short answer: powder coating for manufacturers works best when preparation, masking and timing are agreed before parts arrive. These answers cover suitability, lead times, quotes, recurring work and logistics for production equipment.

blocks.q: Is powder coating suitable for automation equipment?
blocks.a: Yes. Powder coating for manufacturers gives automation frames, guards and bases a hard, uniform finish that resists scratches, coolant and cleaning chemicals. Proper preparation and masking keep moving surfaces and threaded features clean, so parts assemble without rework. This makes it a practical option for powder coating for machine frames, enclosures and guarding that must be installed straight from the shop.

blocks.q: How fast can manufacturers get parts back?
blocks.a: Standard orders are returned in 48 hours. Large or complex frames, heavy sandblasting and special colours can take longer, and we confirm the timing in writing before work starts. If your schedule is fixed, tell us the date you need parts on site and we will plan the work backward from it.

blocks.q: What should I send for a manufacturing powder coating quote?
blocks.a: Send photos or drawings, the metal type, approximate size and weight, quantity, colour code and any surfaces that must stay bare. A sample part helps with complex jobs, and our quote form accepts photo uploads.

blocks.q: Can you handle repeat orders for manufacturer powder coating?
blocks.a: Yes. We record the powder, colour code and prep method for each job, so later batches match earlier ones. Many manufacturers schedule recurring work with us so parts arrive on a predictable cycle. This suits manufacturers who buy powder coating for manufacturing in regular batches alongside their own production.

blocks.q: Do you offer pickup and delivery for manufacturing orders?
blocks.a: Yes. Pickup and delivery details are agreed when we confirm your order. You can also drop parts at our Milton shop between 7 AM and 5 PM, Monday to Friday.
